chunks: Sa'd from Abu Ja'far from his father from Muhammad ibn 'Isa and al-Husayn ibn Sa'id and Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from 'Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): In

regarding a man who becomes junub after raising his head in the final prostration and before the Tashahhud, he said: 'He turns around (ends his prayer), then performs ablution. If he wishes, he returns to the mosque; if he wishes, [he prays] in his house; and if he wishes, he sits wherever he wishes, performs the Tashahhud, then gives the Taslim. And if the impurity occurred after the two testimonies of faith, then his prayer has passed (is valid).'

The appropriate interpretation of this report is to apply it to one who entered his prayer with dry ablution (tayammum), then became junub unintentionally before the two testimonies. For he performs ablution if he has found water, and completes the prayer with the two testimonies, and he is not required to repeat it, just as he is required to complete it if he became junub before that, according to what we clarified in the Book of Purity.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a person becomes junub after the final prostration but before finishing the prayer?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Baqir (AS) via a chain including Zurarah, clarifying that if one breaks ritual purity after the final prostration but before the Tashahhud, they must perform ablution and can complete the prayer from wherever they are, rather than restarting. The text further elucidates a specific scenario for those who prayed with tayammum and later found water, establishing that their prayer remains valid upon performing wudu, a nuance derived from the principle of continuity in worship. This highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the validity of the prayer's core components even when interrupted by minor impurities, provided the essential pillars are maintained.
